item.title: Nigerian newspapers review: [Ebola] FG quarantines high-risk contacts, allays fears of spread
item.description: In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with the Federal Government saying it has intensified efforts to contain Nigeria’s confirmed case of Ebola Virus Disease; placed high-risk contacts in quarantine, isolated other contacts and strengthened preparedness across states as well as health facilities. Another headline features the National Economic Council (NEC) endorsing a 90-day economic action plan proposed by the Federal Ministry of Finance to consolidate gains from President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms. Vanguard also reports that the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) has warned of possible nationwide action following the failure of talks with the Federal Government over workers’ welfare, petrol prices and other labour demands. Moving to another newspaper, The Guardian leads with the Federal Government saying political campaigns, conferences and other major public gatherings can proceed, pending any change in the public health situation amid the confirmed Ebola Virus Disease case in the country. The Punch reports that former President Olusegun Obasanjo accused President Bola Tinubu of making every Nigerian poor by 300 per cent through the devaluation of the naira, saying the policy has turned Nigeria into “the poverty capital of the world.” Lastly, The Nation reports that former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has demanded the immediate publication of the preliminary voters’ register, warning that its reported absence from the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) online portal raises concerns about the credibility of the 2027 general election. In a statement on Friday, the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, said the APC had focused on President Bola Tinubu’s name sounding like ‘Ebola’ instead of explaining what happened to the funds. “They found the rhyme, wrote a lengthy press statement about it and somehow still could not tell Nigerians where the ₦10 billion ordered released for Ebola preparedness is. If only they searched the accounts with the same enthusiasm they brought to the dictionary.” The statement followed an APC response to ADC’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, over the N10bn that the Presidency announced in June had been ordered released for Ebola preparedness. It added that while Ebola destroys lives through disease, Tinubu’s policies had made food and medical care unaffordable and hurt businesses Nigerians had spent years building. Shaibu also said the APC had claimed the money remained “untouched” despite the announcement and demanded clarification on whether it had been released and where it was being held. “Was the money released or was it not? If it was released, where is it held, who controls it, and why has it not been used for the preparedness President Tinubu announced? item.title: UK, Nigeria deepen collaboration on AI governance, digital transformation
item.description: By Juliet Umeh The United Kingdom and Nigeria have strengthened their collaboration on artificial intelligence governance and digital transformation, following a series of engagements involving the British Standards Institution, BSI, and Nigerian government agencies. The engagements included an Executive Workshop on AI Governance and Standards, delivered by BSI in partnership with the National Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics, NCAIR, under the UK Government’s Digital Access Programme. The workshop brought together senior government officials, regulators and technology practitioners to examine how internationally recognised standards can support responsible AI adoption, risk management and oversight in Nigeria. Participants considered standards including ISO/IEC 42001 for AI management systems and ISO/IEC 23894 for AI risk management, as well as approaches to accountability and assurance. The programme culminated in a reception in Abuja attended by policymakers, regulators, standards experts, industry representatives and development partners. Speaking at the event, First Secretary for Economic Partnerships and Digital at the British High Commission, Grace Bell, said AI offered significant opportunities but required strong governance. “Artificial Intelligence presents enormous opportunities for economic growth, innovation and social development. However, realising these benefits requires the right governance frameworks, strong institutions and trusted standards that can underpin safe, secure and responsible adoption,” she said. item.title: NEC Endorses 90-Day Economic Plan To Ease Cost Of Living For Nigerians

item.title: Ministers spend billions to secure appointments, APC spokesman alleges
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Alwan Hassan, a spokesperson for the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, has alleged that some ministers pay billions of naira to secure appointments and subsequently focus on recovering the money. Hassan made the allegation during an interview on Arise News on Thursday, describing ministers as among the most corrupt officials in government and claiming the practice predates the APC administration. “Every time a government goes out, the most criminal elements in government are ministers,” he said. “A lot of ministers pay billions to be appointed, and the first thing they think of is how to recoup that money after being appointed.” “It is the truth about our country and not just APC ministers; it started before the APC,” he said. “The biggest fraudulent people you arrest after every government are ministers.” He also questioned the role of ministers in budget implementation, arguing that the government’s ability to fund approved budgets should be a priority. “Why do we need ministers? Why do we need budget to be given to ministers?” he asked. ‘Power has improved under Tinubu’ Hassan also defended President Bola Tinubu’s performance, saying the administration had taken steps to address challenges in the power sector. He claimed Tinubu had approved more than ₦4tn for electricity meters, arguing that expanding household metering was important to improving electricity supply. “There is no way you fix power issue without having every household powered,” Hassan said. On the use of solar power at the Presidential Villa, Hassan said the government had introduced financing support to help civil servants acquire solar systems. “That is why he [President Tinubu] introduced Credicorp for civil servants to buy their own solar system,” he said. Tinubu will get votes in the north in 2027 Speaking on the 2027 general election, Hassan argued that President Tinubu’s projects in parts of the North would help him win in states such as Bauchi and Kano, where he lost in the 2023 election. “In 2023, Asiwaju was a candidate and not the president. He’s done a lot in places like Kano and done a lot of streets in the North that will translate to votes,” he said. Hassan also cited the renovation of 287 primary schools and more than 4,000 classrooms through the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) as examples of the administration’s achievements. item.title: One Dead, Three Rescued As Building Collapses In Lagos
item.description: One person has been confirmed dead and three others injured after a building collapsed in the Fadeyi area of Lagos State. The incident occurred on Akinola Street, off Ikorodu Road, on Friday morning. An emergency response team carries out a search-and-rescue operation with an excavator at the scene of a building collapse in Lagos State on October 23, 2026. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) said that while the cause of the collapse has yet to be ascertained, emergency responders are making frantic efforts to ascertain the number of people (on-site workers) trapped beneath the collapsed structure. An emergency response team carries out a search-and-rescue operation with an excavator at the scene of a building collapse in Lagos State on October 23, 2026. LASEMA said emergency responders have begun a coordinated search of the incident scene to ensure the prompt rescue of victims trapped under the collapsed building. It also noted that it is managing the incident scene to ensure a successful operation in collaboration with stakeholders, including the LRU paramedics, Lagos State Fire Service, LASASA and the Alabama Division of the Nigeria Police Force. item.title: Maradona death trial verdict set for December 22
item.description: The verdict in the trial over the 2020 death of Argentine football legend Diego Maradona will be delivered on December 22, the court announced Thursday, after six months of hearings. The trial of seven healthcare professionals accused of negligence in the star’s death concluded Thursday with brief statements from Maradona’s daughter and some of the defendants. “I hope my father receives the justice he deserves…like anyone else,” said Dalma Maradona, her voice breaking with emotion. The main defendant in the case, Leopoldo Luque, Maradona’s primary doctor, declared: “I am innocent.” Maradona died at age 60 from heart failure coupled with pulmonary edema. The larger-than-life star, who had a history of substance abuse, was found dead in his bed on November 25, 2020. He was at his residence in Tigre, north of Buenos Aires, rented for his convalescence following minor neurosurgery. His death plunged the country into mourning in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic. – ‘Scapegoat’ – The trial, which began in April, included testimony from more than 70 witnesses. Prosecutors requested prison sentences ranging from four to twelve years for six of the seven defendants, with the heaviest sentence — 12 years — sought for Luque. In closing arguments on Wednesday, Luque’s defense attorneys rejected the prosecution’s argument that Maradona’s death was foreseeable, calling their client a “scapegoat” in the case. Throughout the trial, Luque was by far the most combative defendant, speaking several times when he felt he was being implicated. His legal team played audio recordings, presented scientific articles and even a video of Maradona’s autopsy, provoking the anger of the footballer’s daughters. “It’s easy to attack me because I’m the one who had the most contact with Maradona,” Luque said in court, asserting that “the only one who would defend me would be Diego.” “I cared deeply for him, I loved him, he was my idol and my friend,” he said. The case has revolved around whether the doctors’ decision to allow Maradona to convalesce in a private home, instead of in a hospital, was negligent. The prosecution pointed to the near-total absence of medical equipment, such as a hospital bed, defibrillator or quickly available ambulance as evidence of what they presented as the defendants’ dereliction of duty. Several medical experts testified that Maradona’s caretakers failed to react to key warning signs — he was suffering from edema, tachycardia and had difficulty breathing — in the lead-up to his death. item.content:encoded: The verdict in the trial over the 2020 death of Argentine football legend Diego Maradona will be delivered on December 22, the court announced Thursday, after six months of hearings. The trial of seven healthcare professionals accused of negligence in the star’s death concluded Thursday with brief statements from Maradona’s daughter and some of the defendants. “I hope my father receives the justice he deserves…like anyone else,” said Dalma Maradona, her voice breaking with emotion. The main defendant in the case, Leopoldo Luque, Maradona’s primary doctor, declared: “I am innocent.” Maradona died at age 60 from heart failure coupled with pulmonary edema. The larger-than-life star, who had a history of substance abuse, was found dead in his bed on November 25, 2020. He was at his residence in Tigre, north of Buenos Aires, rented for his convalescence following minor neurosurgery. His death plunged the country into mourning in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic. – ‘Scapegoat’ – The trial, which began in April, included testimony from more than 70 witnesses. Prosecutors requested prison sentences ranging from four to twelve years for six of the seven defendants, with the heaviest sentence — 12 years — sought for Luque. In closing arguments on Wednesday, Luque’s defense attorneys rejected the prosecution’s argument that Maradona’s death was foreseeable, calling their client a “scapegoat” in the case. Throughout the trial, Luque was by far the most combative defendant, speaking several times when he felt he was being implicated. His legal team played audio recordings, presented scientific articles and even a video of Maradona’s autopsy, provoking the anger of the footballer’s daughters. “It’s easy to attack me because I’m the one who had the most contact with Maradona,” Luque said in court, asserting that “the only one who would defend me would be Diego.” “I cared deeply for him, I loved him, he was my idol and my friend,” he said. The case has revolved around whether the doctors’ decision to allow Maradona to convalesce in a private home, instead of in a hospital, was negligent. The prosecution pointed to the near-total absence of medical equipment, such as a hospital bed, defibrillator or quickly available ambulance as evidence of what they presented as the defendants’ dereliction of duty. Several medical experts testified that Maradona’s caretakers failed to react to key warning signs — he was suffering from edema, tachycardia and had difficulty breathing — in the lead-up to his death. item.title: FG intensifies response to confirmed Ebola case in FCT
item.description: The Federal Government says it has deepened public health response following the confirmation of an Ebola virus disease (EVD) case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Oct. 20, 2026. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a statement issued by Mr Oluwafemi Adeniyi, the ministry’s spokesman on Thursday. According to him, such a response to the confirmed case of the disease in the FCT is coming against the backdrop of information provided by the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare. Adeniyi said, “The patient is a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda. “She was subsequently admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received medical care for several days before her diagnosis was confirmed; the patient is currently in isolation and receiving treatment.” He narrated that the government, through the Federal Ministry of Health and the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), is working with the FCT Health Services Secretariat to contain the infection and prevent further transmission. Also, that contact tracing operations had commenced with 44 close contacts identified for monitoring and appropriate public health follow-up. This, according to him, means response teams are working to identify, assess and monitor individuals who may have been exposed to the virus, including healthcare workers, patients, carers and persons linked to the patient’s travel. “Government is also coordinating surveillance, laboratory testing and other essential response activities in line with established public health protocols,” he said. He mentioned that the measures taken by government are intended to facilitate early identification of potential cases, strengthen infection prevention and control, and minimise risks of further transmission. He reiterated the government’s commitment to safeguarding the health and well-being of Nigerians and all residents, urging the public to cooperate with such moves. “Members of the public are urged to remain calm, avoid speculation and misinformation, and adhere strictly to advisories issued by the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the NCDC and relevant health authorities. “The public is encouraged to rely exclusively on verified information from official government channels,” he said. He reaffirmed that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs would liaise with relevant national institutions and other stakeholders, as necessary, in supporting the government’s coordinated response to the public health situation. He further assured that an update would be issued through official channels, as verified information becomes available, while thanking the public and all stakeholders for their cooperation. item.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos face a stern test against defending champions Korea DPR on Friday as they seek to secure a place in the Round of 16 at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Korea DPR, two-time champions since the competition began in New Zealand in 2008, have been impressive, winning their opening two matches to top Group B. The North Koreans have scored 12 goals and conceded only one, underlining their attacking strength as they pursue another title. Nigeria, bronze medallists in 2022, are seeking to keep their campaign alive after losing 2-1 to Poland before recovering with a 2-0 victory over tournament debutants Puerto Rico. The Flamingos will need a disciplined performance against the defending champions, with qualification for the knockout stage still within reach. A win or draw would guarantee Nigeria’s progress, while a defeat would leave their chances dependent on the outcome of the Poland-Puerto Rico match and the applicable tiebreakers. The two teams have met twice at the U-17 Women’s World Cup, with Nigeria winning 3-2 in 2010 before Korea DPR recorded a 3-0 victory in 2016. Coach Akeem Busari and his players will need to remain defensively organised and take their chances against a North Korean side that has dominated its group matches. item.title: One dead, three rescued in Lagos building collapse
item.description: The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) has confirmed one death and the rescue of three adult males following the collapse of a two-storey building under construction in Fadeyi, Lagos. The Permanent Secretary of LASEMA, Dr Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, confirmed in a statement made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Friday in Lagos. Oke-Osanyintolu ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌​⁠​‍‍‍‌‌​said the incident occurred in the early hours of Friday at Akinola Street, by Fadeyi Bus Stop, off Ikorodu Road. He said search and rescue operations were ongoing to determine whether more persons were trapped beneath the rubble. He said the agency received a distress call at 12:10 a.m., prompting the immediate activation of its Cobra Response Team from Onipanu Base. According to him, the team arrived at the scene at 12:12 a.m. and discovered that the building under construction had collapsed, with construction workers suspected to be trapped beneath the debris. Oke-Osanyintolu said search and rescue operations commenced immediately, with safety measures put in place to protect victims and emergency responders. He added that groaning sounds were heard beneath the rubble during the operation, indicating possible survivors. He said the agency deployed an excavator to facilitate the search and rescue operation. Oke-Osanyintolu said the rescued victims received immediate pre-hospital care from LASEMA paramedics and the Lagos State Ambulance Service (LASAMBUS) before being transferred to hospital. He listed the responders at the scene as the LASEMA Response Team, Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, LASAMBUS and officers of the Nigeria Police Force from Alagbon Division. He said the cause of the collapse had yet to be determined and would be investigated by relevant regulatory agencies. He commiserated with the family of the deceased and wished the rescued victims a speedy recovery. He also reiterated the government’s commitment to tackling substandard construction and strengthening monitoring and enforcement in collaboration with the Lagos State Building Control Agency to prevent similar incidents. item.title: No Electricity, No Vote: Service Chaos Tests South Africa’s ANC
item.description: Thick cables snaked along footpaths in a township outside South Africa’s wealthiest city, Johannesburg, where 180 households have relied on illegal electricity connections for more than 20 years. Angry about the authorities’ failure to get them properly connected to the grid, residents have resolved to turn their backs on their ANC-led municipality at the November 4 local elections, a test for the once-majority party that has been bleeding support for more than two decades. “We have made a collective decision: no electricity, no vote,” said community leader Lesiba Rankapole, 59. For other communities across the country, complaints feeding disillusionment with African National Congress (ANC) municipalities include failures to provide water or collect garbage, as well as mismanagement and corruption. “We know it is illegal, but we had no choice because we cannot live without electricity,” said Rankapole of the wires that take power from another area of Katlehong, a sprawling semi-urban area on the edge of Johannesburg. “Our children cannot progress without electricity.” It is “obvious we are not going to vote, especially for the ANC”, said another resident, Enock Majola, 57, who pointed out illegal dumping sites. “I was born ANC, but today I do not want anyone to tell me about the ANC because I am suffering,” he said. For other communities across the country, complaints feeding disillusionment with African National Congress (ANC) municipalities include failures to provide water or collect garbage, as well as mismanagement and corruption. “We know it is illegal, but we had no choice because we cannot live without electricity,” said Rankapole of the wires that take power from another area of Katlehong, a sprawling semi-urban area on the edge of Johannesburg. “Our children cannot progress without electricity.” It is “obvious we are not going to vote, especially for the ANC”, said another resident, Enock Majola, 57, who pointed out illegal dumping sites. “I was born ANC, but today I do not want anyone to tell me about the ANC because I am suffering,” he said. Residents fill up water buckets from a communal tap as another washes her laundry next to a Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) municipal election poster in Alexandra, near Johannesburg, on October 5, 2026. (Photo by EMMANUEL CROSET / AFP) Sliding support At the heart of South Africa’s anti-apartheid struggle, the ANC — the party of jailed liberation hero-turned-president Nelson Mandela — took nearly 70 percent of the national vote in 2004. It fell below 50 percent for the first time at the last municipal elections in 2021, when it won 46 percent of votes and retained control of nearly half the municipalities. At the 2024 national vote, it managed just over 40 percent and was forced to accept a coalition government. The party’s weakness has emboldened spin-offs such as the uMkhonto weSizwe Party (MKP) led by former president Jacob Zuma that is contesting local elections for the first time this year. Elsewhere in Katlehong, Meshack Twala was digging to reach a blocked pipe at a house surrounded by sewage. “How do we go and vote when our entire street has been experiencing persistent sewage problems?” he said, conceding, though, that if he did make it to a voting station, he would plump for the ANC. “Changing to other parties would not feel right,” the 58-year-old said. Municipal elections generally attract low turnout, which “hurts the ANC”, said political analyst Sethulego Matebesi. But the vote will give parties an “idea of where their support base is” as they look towards the 2029 national poll, he said. Matebesi predicted no party would win an outright majority and the country would be “full swing” into coalition-building and hung municipalities. People walk near a puddle of water from a leaking pipe in central Johannesburg, on October 7, 2026. (Photo by ILARIA FINIZIO / AFP) Johannesburg: the big prize Of the 257 councils up for grabs, the fight for control is particularly intense in Johannesburg, an economic dynamo of more than 4.8 million people and the face of Africa’s most industrialised nation. South Africa’s stark inequalities are laid bare in the Alexandra township from where skyscrapers of the Sandton business district — reputed to be the richest square mile on the continent — are visible. Heaps of rubbish, potholes and sewage flows lined the roads. “The ANC has been governing for years, but we have not seen any changes in Alexandra,” said maintenance worker Patrick Saohatse, 45. He said he would give his vote to the liberal Democratic Alliance, the second-largest party in the ruling coalition after the ANC. Already in charge of the country’s second city Cape Town, the DA has pushed hard on ANC service delivery failures and mismanagement in a campaign that started more than a year ago. “Another five years of corruption and collapsing infrastructure will push our city beyond recovery,” said mayoral candidate, 75-year-old Helen Zille, at a recent rally. Less than two weeks before polling day, the ANC was yet to choose its candidate amid lacklustre campaigning. “If you look at the situation in and around Johannesburg, there are reasons for people not to be happy,” the party’s head of elections, Mdumiseni Ntuli, told AFP. “We have made mistakes and accepted our shortcomings, but ANC remains a better option for people,” he said, urging voters to cast their ballots. Running for a second chance to be Johannesburg mayor is the leader of the centre-right Action SA, Herman Mashaba, 67. “Our refuse collection is irregular; our streets have no lights… I keep asking myself, what on earth is happening?” he said to AFP. We should actually listen to them.” As far as Lufadeju is concerned, the upsides of the generation’s characteristics far outweigh the downsides. Asked to comment on the expulsion and suspension of the Madonna University students, she told Vanguard, “Is there an actual law against dancing? Seriously, I am asking not rhetorically. I might be wrong.” Your Negativity, Their Creativity Despite the admiration for their resilience, most members of older generations regard Gen Z with wariness, at best. The 15 Madonna University students, despite the initial public outrage, have nevertheless garnered considerable sympathy over the disciplinary actions taken against them, particularly given that they were all in their fifth and final year at the School of Nursing. Amnesty International has weighed in on the expulsion and suspension of the TikTok dancers, describing the actions as “disproportionate”. The organisation’s published statement reads: “Imposing heavy-handed academic or disciplinary sanctions would terminate the academic progress of the affected students. The students have the rights to freedom of expression, academic freedom and education. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 23, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian Naira exchanged at around N1,330.95 to the US Dollar at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM). The official window opened with early spot transactions hovering around N1,330.95 to N1,332.00 per dollar, maintaining relative stability following recent daily fluctuations. In the unofficial parallel market, street traders and Bureau De Change (BDC) operators across major commercial hubs, including Lagos and Abuja, quoted buying rates around N1,360 to N1,365 per dollar, while selling rates traded between N1,375 and N1,380 per dollar. The gap between the official NFEM rate and the parallel market continues to reflect ongoing demand from retail buyers, small business importers, and individuals seeking foreign currency for international travel and tuition payments. At current trading levels, exchanging $100 yields approximately N133,095 through official banking and NFEM channels, compared to up to N138,000 when purchased through parallel market operators. Market participants attribute current rate stability to sustained diaspora remittance inflows alongside foreign portfolio interest in domestic yield instruments. item.title: NYSC kidnap: DSS witness exposes how suspects were identified
item.description: By Chidi Nkwopara OWERRI — A Department of State Services, DSS, operative yesterday told an Imo State High Court how 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps, NYSC, members were abducted at gunpoint while travelling to orientation camps, as hearing began in the case against three alleged kidnappers. The witness, Ikechukwu Emmanuel, who investigated the incident, said the victims and one of the bus drivers identified the three defendants during an identification parade. The defendants, Usman Aliyu, alias Chonge; Babangida Aliyu; and Mohamed Ali, alias Smallie Pepper, are standing trial on a three-count charge of conspiracy, hostage-taking and unlawful possession of firearms in suit number HOU/22C/2026. Testifying before Justice Emeka Orafu, the DSS operative said the incident occurred at about 6.30am on October 1, 2026, when the 20 prospective corps members were travelling in two buses from Ibadan to NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. He told the court that armed men wielding AK-47 rifles attacked the buses and took all 20 passengers hostage, moving them into the bush. According to the witness, security agencies in Imo State, including the DSS, launched operations using human and technical intelligence to track the kidnappers and secure the victims’ release. He said the hostages were eventually released after the payment of ransom demanded by the kidnappers, while investigations continued. Emmanuel further told the court that intelligence reports indicated that the suspects had moved to Rivers and Abia states, leading to their arrest between October 10 and 14, 2026. Explaining the identification process, the witness said the three defendants were placed among 10 other persons during an identification parade. He said the abducted prospective corps members and one of the bus drivers identified them. The witness also told the court that Usman Aliyu, in his confessional statement, said 11 persons participated in the kidnap operation. The Imo State Director of Public Prosecutions, Mr Martins Udolwu, led the prosecution team, while Mr Nnaemeka S.C. Adipo and Mr Paschal Ofoma represented the defendants. After the witness’s evidence-in-chief, Justice Orafu adjourned the case to October 27, 28 and 29, 2026, for continuation of hearing. The judge urged the defence to be ready to cross-examine the witness immediately after the conclusion of his evidence-in-chief, stressing that he did not want the trial to extend into the new year. “The Defence must be ready to cross-examine the witness immediately he is done with his evidence in chief,” the judge said. item.title: Nollywood actor Francis Duru dies at 57
item.description: Veteran Nollywood actor Francis Duru has died at the age of 57 following a brief illness, his family has announced. The family announced his death in a statement posted on the actor’s official Instagram page in the early hours of Friday, expressing appreciation to fans and well-wishers for their prayers and support. “We, the family of Francis Duru, regret to announce his passing following a brief illness. “We appreciate your prayers, love, and understanding. May his soul rest in perfect peace. Amen,” the statement read. Duru is survived by his wife, Adokiye, and children Duru, who began his acting career in 1989, became widely known for his role as Ahanna in Rattlesnake , the 1995 film produced by the late filmmaker Amaka Igwe. His death comes months after he dismissed reports that he was battling a life-threatening illness, describing footage circulating online in June as false. In a video posted on Instagram in response to the reports, the actor rejected claims about his health and criticised those circulating the footage. Born on July 27, 1969, in Cameroon to Nigerian parents from Imo State, Duru completed his primary and secondary education in Cameroon before moving to Nigeria for university studies. He studied Theatre Arts at the University of Port Harcourt, Rivers State, graduating with a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1996. Duru made his film debut in Missing Mark in 1989, in a production directed by the late Ndubuisi Oko. His performance in Rattlesnake later established him as a recognised face in Nollywood. Over his decades-long career, he featured in several Nigerian films, including Blood Money (1997), Stigma (2013) and Mboputa (2020). In 2020, he won the Best Actor in a Leading Role (Igbo) award at the Best of Nollywood Awards for his performance in Mboputa . He also received the United Nations Ambassador of Peace award in 2007 in recognition of his influence on young people. Duru served as interim president of the Actors Guild of Nigeria in 2010 and was nominated for Best Actor in a Supporting Role at the Africa Movie Academy Awards that year. item.title: State Police: 24 states approve bill; Lagos, 9 northern, 2 southern states dilly-dally

Kaduna ‌‌Assembly endorses constitutional state police Kaduna State House of Assembly, yesterday, joined approving states by unanimously endorsing proposed amendments to 15 sections of the 1999 Constitution to pave the way for the establishment of state police. The Chairman House Committee on Information , Mr Henry Marah, disclosed this while briefing journalists on the House proceedings in Kaduna. He said the proposed state police system would strengthen community security, improve protection of lives and property, and create employment opportunities for youths. According to him, the current security structure limits state governments’ ability to directly hold police authorities accountable for security failures. He said the proposed system would provide a legal framework for community-based security initiatives and strengthen local responses to banditry and other crimes. Marah said the Assembly would formulate appropriate laws to guide the operations and welfare of state police personnel when the proposal takes effect. He assured that funding would be prioritised, even if the state had to reduce spending on other projects. “Without security, you cannot even go to the farm or go to work,” he said, stressing that protecting human lives should take precedence over infrastructure development. The lawmaker urged residents to support the proposed state police system, saying improved security would enable farmers to return to their farms and harvest their produce without fear of kidnapping. Abia assembly concurs Similarly, the Deputy Speaker, Abia State House of Assembly, Austin Nmeregini, told Vanguard, earlier yesterday, that the Abia lawmakers were at the verge of passing the Bill. He disclosed that the Bill received the support of the lawmakers during their Executive session, hinting that they were proceeding into plenary where it would be passed into law. However, Speaker Austin Nmeregini, told Vanguard later in the day that the bill was passed by unanimous vote Bill yet to be received — Gombe lawmaker In Gombe, the Chairman, House Committee on Appropriation, Aliyu Baba Manu, said the bill has not been officially presented on the floor of the House. According to Manu, the bill has neither been formally tabled nor received by the House for consideration. He added that upon receipt, the bill would be referred to the appropriate committee responsible for police matters for further legislative action. Speaking in a like manner, Deputy Speaker of Gombe House of Assembly said he is unaware of the bill. Ebonyi to pass bill soon — Speaker The Speaker of the Ebonyi State House of Assembly, Moses Ije Odunwa, has said the Assembly will soon pass the State Police Bill. Odunwa disclosed that lawmakers had commenced deliberations on the bill and were close to completing the process, subject to necessary scrutiny. He said the proposed legislation was aimed at strengthening the protection of lives and property in Ebonyi State and Nigeria at large. The Speaker recalled that Ebonyi State had supported the establishment of state police during the National Assembly’s constitutional review engagement, where the state government and Assembly made submissions in favour of decentralised policing. “We have started deliberating on the bill, and we are very close to its passage,” Odunwa said. Action on bill delayed in Ondo In Ondo State, the Chairman, House Committee on Information, Olatunji Oshati, said the draft has been forwarded to all 26 members of the Assembly to study and return with their resolutions for debate at plenary. “Yes, we have received the draft from the National Assembly. We have read it on the floor of the House and subsequently distributed it to the 26 members of the Assembly to study. The lawmakers are expected to study the document and return with their inputs for full deliberation at the next plenary. “The State House of Assembly, after thorough discussion under matters of urgent public importance, will add our inputs before returning it to the National Assembly. “I want to assure that all these will be done within a short period. We won’t delay; we will soon send the State Assembly’s inputs to the National Assembly,” he said. He however assured that the bill will be passed after the plenary sitting on Monday by the members. According to him, “the plenary on Monday will decide when the bill will be passed into law.” Kogi assembly yet to sit In Kogi State, the House of Assembly is yet to sit on the State police amendment bill. However, the Assembly admitted some weeks ago that it had received the transmitted copy, but a day was yet to be slated for its debate. The Members had adjourned to attend an international conference in Rwanda, “maybe by the next adjourned date, answers to your questions will be provided”, Mr. Aka Bayo, Deputy clerk, Administration stated. Why Lagos Assembly is yet to ratify the Bill — Lawmaker The Chairman of the Lagos State House of Assembly Committee on Information and Strategy, Mr. Stephen Ogundipe, said the House will reconvene next week to ratify the bill. Ogundipe disclosed that the Assembly is currently in recess but assured that lawmakers would resume plenary next week to consider the bill and take the necessary legislative action. He explained that the planned ratification would form part of the Assembly’s legislative responsibilities upon resumption, although he did not provide further details on the specific provisions of the bill. “The ratification process will be a key stage in determining the bill’s legislative status, subject to the applicable procedures of the House. The Assembly is expected to provide further information as deliberations resume and lawmakers proceed with their legislative business next week”, he said. item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has raised the alarm over the alleged failure of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to publish the preliminary voters’ register for public scrutiny, warning that the lapse could undermine confidence in the 2027 general election. Atiku said Nigerians could not verify the commission’s claim that more than 103 million voters had been registered when the register was reportedly unavailable on its online portal during the October 9 to 15 inspection period. In a statement on Thursday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku demanded the immediate publication of the register, questioning conflicting accounts of when it was displayed and raising concerns about safeguards against electoral fraud. “INEC has announced more than 103 million registered voters. Nigerians went to its portal to inspect the names and found an empty page. That is an outrage. A figure cannot answer an objection. A press announcement cannot tell a voter whether her name has been omitted. Show Nigerians the register,” he said. Atiku also questioned reports that INEC’s chairman had said on October 5 that the public display had already been completed, despite the commission’s subsequent announcement of an October 9 to 15 inspection period. “Which statement is true? Where was the register published? For seven full days, or for no days at all? INEC must produce the dates, the links and the records of access,” he demanded. The former vice president further raised concerns over Section 63(2) of the Electoral Act 2026, which permits a returning officer to count a ballot paper without INEC’s official mark if satisfied that it came from a book supplied to the polling unit. He argued that the provision required enforceable safeguards to establish the origin of such ballot papers and prevent counterfeit votes. “Nigerians cannot be denied access to the voters’ register before election day and then be asked to accept unmarked ballot papers after voting. INEC must set out enforceable safeguards against counterfeit ballots, and the National Assembly must close any loophole that leaves the authenticity of a vote to an officer’s unsupported assurance,” Atiku said. The ADC campaign council also faulted INEC for failing to respond to inquiries about the identities of companies awarded contracts to print sensitive election materials, raising a separate question about transparency in the handling of critical electoral materials. item.description: Bournemouth pulled off a sensational 3-0 home victory over 10-man AC Milan on Thursday to make it three wins from their opening three games in the Europa League. Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier converted first-half penalties to put Bournemouth firmly in control against AC Milan, one of Europe’s leading clubs. Milan goalkeeper and skipper Mike Maignan was red carded early on for a foul on Tyler Adams and his side never fully recovered. Amine Adli scored a sublime 84th free-kick to make it 3-0, the Premier League side having opened their inaugural Europa League campaign with victory at Real Sociedad followed by a 3-0 home win over Sturm Graz last week. Bournemouth’s Premier League rivals Crystal Palace were held 2-2 by Beskitas in Istanbul, while Scottish giants Celtic suffered a third successive defeat, going down 2-1 to Celta Vigo. AC Milan’s Italian defender #33 Davide Bartesaghi reacts after the UEFA Europa League, league stage football match between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium in Bournemouth, southern England on October 22, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP) Bayer Leverkusen, however, also made it three straight wins with a Jonas Hofmann double earning a 2-0 away win at OFI Crete as both Juventus and Sunderland lost ground in Thursday’s third matchday. The once mighty Hungarian side Ferencvaros kept pace with Leverkusen on nine points thumping Portuguese outfit Torreense 4-1, while Belgium’s Union Saint-Gilloise won 4-0 against Israeli outfit Hapoel Be’er Sheva. Saint-Gilloise, Sunderland and Juve all have seven points from three games.
